comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
Fixed on `main3` (slot 3 of the 2026-09-02 parallel round): `fix: a window says on screen the panes it is drawing`.

## The restore path was not the cause

The card asked to settle that first, and it is settled the other way. A test now drives a real daemon, splits a tab into four panes, relaunches onto the saved arrangement and asks `ReadWindow`: all four report `on_screen`, and did before any change. `session::window()` recomputes the view and the roster on every read - no cache - so "the restore never recomputes" is out.

## What was wrong is the derivation, and it had no coverage at all

`RosterPane::on_screen` came from `View::showing()`, which walked each region's published *tree*. A tree is how a tab's panes are arranged; it is not which panes are drawn, and it goes absent for two reasons that have nothing to do with the screen:

- the daemon has not published one yet, and
- the one it published disagrees with the tab's pane list, so `arranges()` withholds it.

In both, the shell is documented to leave its surfaces alone - so the window is drawing panes while the answer says nothing is on screen. That is the contradiction the card's last bullet names, and it was reachable from the derivation alone.

The new rule: **a region shows a tab, and a tab on screen has its panes on screen.** A zoom is the one thing that covers a pane without closing its tab, so a zoomed region reports the one pane filling it. Always defined, which the old rule was not.

## The gap that let this happen

`corpus/conformance/composition.json` pinned every region's tree in all 51 cases and never pinned what the window said was on screen. It does now. Forty-five of the expectations follow mechanically from the tree lines that were already reviewed - a published tree names exactly the tab's panes, since `arranges()` compares them for equality - and six are hand-written with their reasons: the ones where a tree is withheld, which are exactly where the answer moved.

## The reported shape, honestly

Exactly one pane on screen and the rest hidden is the zoom signature in the old code, and a withheld tree gives *zero*. The measurement in the card shows one. So either that window had a region reporting a zoom, or it had a second region the excerpt does not show. Both are covered by the new rule, and `muster window --json` now carries `zoomed` on each region (added in the `a_2IZE3PiGe` commit), which is the field that would have made this a read rather than an investigation.

Not exercised here: `./dev --contract`, which is the tier that could reproduce the original window.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
After a window reopens onto a saved arrangement, `muster window` reports every pane in the visible tab as hidden except the one holding the keyboard. All of them are being drawn.

Measured on 0.4.1, a window restored from `window.toml` onto a tab holding four panes:

    muster window --json
      p20970gz3s  tab=t206y99cay  on_screen=False   investigations · claude
      p206y9p61r  tab=t206y99cay  on_screen=True    chicago · claude       <- has the keyboard
      p2073ed9cw  tab=t206y99cay  on_screen=False   goat-dt · claude
      p2090j2nvj  tab=t206y99cay  on_screen=False   goat-dt

The run log for the same launch, four bridges at four different sizes - a real four-way split, not one pane:

    21:33:22  bridge.start   w4:p1  164x107
    21:33:22  bridge.start   w4:p3   98x37
    21:33:22  bridge.start   w4:pA   64x37
    21:33:22  bridge.start   w4:pB  164x34
    21:33:22  pane.typeable  p206y9p61r, p2073ed9cw, p20970gz3s, p2090j2nvj
    21:33:23  bridge.frame.first  x4

Four panes bridged, four painting frames, four typeable. Three of them reported hidden. Still wrong ten seconds later, so it is not a reconcile that has yet to arrive.

The single region names one pane:

    [[region]]
    daemon = "devenv"
    pane = "p206y9p61r"
    tab = "t206y99cay"

`Region::pane` is documented as *"the pane in this region Muster's keyboard feeds while the region is focused"* - which pane takes keystrokes, not which panes are drawn. `on_screen` looks to be derived from it, and the two are only the same thing when a region shows exactly one pane.

Not reproduced in a window that has been running a while: earlier in the same session, the same tab with three panes reported all three on screen. Whatever computes this appears to be right once something has reconciled and wrong on the restore path, which is worth pinning down before fixing - the bug may be that the restore never recomputes rather than that the derivation is wrong.

## Why it matters beyond a wrong word

`on_screen` is not cosmetic. It is what tells you an agent needs surfacing, and it is what an agent driving Muster reads to decide whether a pane needs bringing into view. A pane wrongly marked hidden invites something to go and surface a pane that is already in front of the user, and `muster window` is the surface with no other way to check.

It also undermines what 0.4.0 shipped. `e9398e6` added the sidebar mark for which tabs share the screen, built on this same flag - so that mark is wrong on the same path.

## Reproducing it

1. Open a window with a tab holding several panes in a split.
2. Quit Muster and reopen it, so the arrangement is restored from `window.toml`.
3. `muster window --json`. Every pane in the visible tab reads `on_screen: false` except the one with the keyboard, while all of them are visibly drawn.
4. The run log for that launch shows a `bridge.start` and a `bridge.frame.first` for each of them, at different sizes.

## Validating a fix

- Every pane a region is drawing reports `on_screen: true`, immediately after a restore and not only once something else has reconciled.
- A pane in a tab that is genuinely off screen still reports false - the flag has to keep meaning something.
- The sidebar's shared-screen mark from `e9398e6` is correct on the restore path too.
- A bridge with a first frame and a pane reporting `on_screen: false` is a contradiction worth a test, since it is exactly what this bug looks like from outside.
title: 👻 A restored window reports every drawn pane as hidden but the keyboard's
